draft.title: Parts of a plant cell
card: Plant cells have a nucleus, cell membrane and cytoplasm, as animal cells do. They also have three extra parts.
Cell wall
a rigid layer outside the cell membrane. It supports the cell and gives it a fixed shape.
Chloroplasts
small green parts where photosynthesis happens. Photosynthesis is how a plant makes food using light energy.
Large vacuole
a big space that stores water. When it is full, it presses on the cell wall and keeps the cell firm.
draft.remember: Plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole as well.

a.q: Which part of a plant cell is the site of photosynthesis?
opts: Chloroplasts
Cell wall
Large vacuole
Nucleus
a.why: Chloroplasts are where photosynthesis happens. The cell wall is tempting because it is also found only in plant cells, but it supports the cell and does not make food.

b.q: A lettuce left out of water goes limp. Which change in its cells best explains why the leaf loses its firmness?
opts: The large vacuoles lose water and press less on the walls
The chloroplasts stop making cell walls
The nucleus stops holding the cell in shape
The cell walls lose their rigid outer layer
b.why: A full vacuole presses on the cell wall and keeps the cell firm. When the vacuoles lose water, this pressure drops and the leaf goes limp. The cell wall is tempting, but it is rigid and stays in place, so the loss of water is the cause.
b.clue: Think about what the stored water is pressing against.

b.best: The large vacuoles lose water and press less on the walls

problems.detail: Why (a) says the cell wall is 'found only in plant cells'. Fungi, bacteria and many algae also have cell walls. It would be accurate to say plant cells have one and animal cells do not.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer that matches the card. The explanation for question a wrongly says cell walls are found only in plant cells, when fungi and bacteria have them too.
